reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
After leaving Grandma Naengmyeon Restaurant in Daehakro, I was reasonably full, but headed to Suyu Gombo Naengmyeon Restaurant, the second destination among the cost-effective cold noodle restaurants I saw on YouTube.

I think I've heard the name Gombonaengmyeon somewhere before. I don't know if it's the same house or if there are several stores with the same name, but the name of the store seems like it's a good restaurant. I was a little disappointed by the ordinaryness of the grandmother's naengmyeon restaurant, so I headed there with high expectations, but the store was located in the back of the neighborhood, so after going a bit deeper, Gombonaengmyeon finally appeared.

When I entered the store, there were a decent number of customers in the small shop, and I heard that the whole dumplings that they make themselves were delicious, but I was feeling too full, so if I like cold noodles, I decided to stop by again and try them, and asked for the bibim cold noodles.

The word “Self Service” was written all over the store, and there was a space with a table inside the open door near the kitchen.

After waiting for some time, they finally brought me a good volume of bibim naengmyeon and hot broth that was being heated in a kettle on a burner at the entrance of the store. When I first tasted the hot broth, I thought it was made with beef bones. It felt like the seolleongtang at Grandma Naengmyeon Restaurant. It was a clear type, different from the hot broth, and the subtle taste of beef beef bones was different from what I expected from a common B-grade cold noodle restaurant, so it felt new and good.

It has a good volume and is sprinkled with so many sesame seeds that it gives off a fragrant sesame scent. It reminds me of the old Pungnap-dong Yucheon naengmyeon, but the pickled radish topped with toppings feels different.

After cutting it with scissors and mixing it well, I tasted it. The noodles felt like a thin version of jjolmyeon, were springy, and were only moderately spicy. It felt like I was eating something made at home, but it also had a subtle sourness and the nutty taste of the sesame seeds was too much, so it felt far from the specialness I had expected. Plus, the volume was good, so I was worried whether I would be able to eat it all.

There is an aunt in the kitchen, and the lady boss walks back and forth between the kitchen and the hall. She is the kind and friendly type, and I hear her say that she serves dumplings as a service to customers who order take-out cold noodles.

I barely finished eating the slightly sour bibim naengmyeon, got up, paid the bill, and went out.

I stopped by because I thought it was a hidden B-grade cold noodle restaurant, but by my standards, it was just about the same as a cold noodle restaurant in the neighborhood. I'm not sure if the whole dumplings would be delicious, but it was below expectations, but the volume was good and there was a friendly female owner, so I decided it was okay.

However, there is no intention to revisit.

reviews.author: Traveller Jun
reviews.text:
since1997. The advantage is the interior that shows traces of time and the affordable price. My grandmother kept sweeping and wiping it, so it was pretty neat. A house with a lot of history that everyone in the know has already been to. The menus are similar to Pocha. Self-serve alcohol and water. Cash only. Ordered lungar sugure hotpot and chicken gizzard stew. Beautifully sliced ​​cucumbers and red pepper paste came out first. The portion of Lungpasgure is quite generous. Spicy and heavy internal flavor of garlic and perilla seed powder. A snack that reminds you more of alcohol than rice. The chicken gizzard is standard with onions and cabbage. Here's a bottle of soju and a drink. Even if you eat it all, it's 25,000 won haha. Great value for money.

I had a good time eating.

reviews.text:
I saw on the internet that it was a half-price discount with a multi-child card, but it was different in that it actually only applies to children with three children. However, when I went there, I was more satisfied with the place than I expected.

Visited in January 2025. Receive a discount with the Dadungi Card.

reviews.author: Jamie B
reviews.text: There are a lot of things to experience and play with your child.

reviews.author: Kong King
reviews.text:
During the coronavirus pandemic, we operated on a reservation system, but now the reservation system is no longer available.
At facilities related to Seoul, benefits for multiple children are available even if there are only two children, but here, benefits for multiple children are still available only when there are three or more children.
Still, it’s great to have a facility like this in northeastern Seoul. I had a great time playing with the kids.

reviews.author: Chelly
reviews.text:
Because it was an individual visit, I visited without making a reservation.
There is an underground parking lot and a paid parking lot outside.
When I went, the underground parking lot was full, so I parked in the outside parking lot.
The admission fee is 5,000 won for the general public and other regions. There are various facilities that children will enjoy, and there is a space on the first basement floor where they can eat packed food.
There was also a water park open in the summer behind the building.

reviews.author: Life traveler
reviews.text:
I found this museum because my child said he wanted to explore it. There are a variety of things to see and experience inside. You can enjoy the 4D Ghost Bus on a graphically processed multiple screen with moving chairs, and on the first basement floor, Dooly videos are shown according to the timetable like in a theater. On the 3rd floor, there is a small children's playground, a cafe, and souvenirs for sale. The rooftop is set up like a lounge so you can sunbathe on sunny days haha.
Children love the cute Dooly characters decorated everywhere.
